correctness.rationale: Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of one coordinate gives the three conditional laws. Conditional-expectation contraction yields the support box, and residual orthogonality gives the exact variance-speed defects. If one defect is zero, continuity and invariance force the corresponding coordinate to be constant along every support trajectory; the constant-sine level then forces the next coordinate constant, cyclically making every support point an equilibrium. The packaged checker verifies the exact residual expansions and summed algebraic budget.

value.rationale: The Thomas system is explicitly organized as a cyclic nonlinear feedback circuit, so conditioning each drive on its receiving damped coordinate is intrinsic to the model rather than an arbitrary statistic. The theorem converts that architecture into three exact stationary calibration laws valid separately on every compact invariant component, including coexisting periodic or chaotic components. The speed defects provide measurable nonequilibrium activity diagnostics with a complete equilibrium equality class, while the support box supplies a direct stationary consistency check. This complements, rather than repeats, the literature on bifurcation, stability, diffusion, and attractor dimension.
